notes: net::textproto: Lines, continued lines, response codes, dot reader/writer, MIME headers with Go validation and explicit budgets; Pipeline, Conn (full duplex over one stream), NewConn, Dial and Go's error texts; UTF-8 text only (byte variants exist for lines); tools/textproto_check.py compares framing, error text and loopback Cmd/ReadResponse transcripts with Go

CanonicalMIMEHeaderKey.note: Go's exact rules (invalid keys are returned unchanged); compared with Go by tools/textproto_check.py (K).

Conn.note: A Reader, a Writer and a Pipeline over one Stream (TcpStream, UnixStream or a boxed net::Conn) whose reads and writes take &self, so the halves work from different threads (Conn::into_parts); transcripts compared with Go by tools/textproto_check.py (X).

Conn.Close.note: Closes the stream (shutdown for TcpStream/UnixStream); buffered writes are not flushed, as in Go.

Conn.Cmd.note: Takes the line to send (pass format_args!) and returns the id as u64; sequencing as Go.

Conn.Pipeline.note: Go embeds Pipeline; its methods are on this public field.

Conn.Reader.note: Go embeds Reader; its methods are on this public field.

Conn.Writer.note: Go embeds Writer; its methods are on this public field.

Dial.note: Over rust_stdlib::net::dial; returns Conn<Box<dyn net::Conn>> and the net error unchanged.

Error.note: Go's *Error is ResponseError (textproto::Error is this module's error enum); Error::Response holds it. Text is %03d %q, compared with Go by tools/textproto_check.py (X).

Error.Error.note: impl Display for ResponseError gives Go's text.

MIMEHeader.note: Ordered map of canonical keys to value lists. Go's plain map also allows direct access with non-canonical keys; use raw_values, iter and into_map.

MIMEHeader.Get.note: Returns None where Go returns the empty string for a missing key or an empty value list; an existing empty value is Some(""). Option stands for Go's "" (Rust-shaped).

MIMEHeader.Values.note: A missing key gives an empty slice; Go returns a nil slice, which Rust cannot tell from an empty one.

NewConn.note: Takes a Stream instead of an io.ReadWriteCloser.

NewReader.note: Takes any BufRead instead of a *bufio.Reader.

NewWriter.note: Takes any Write instead of a *bufio.Writer; print_line and the dot writer flush where Go flushes.

Pipeline.note: Shareable between threads (all methods take &self); ids are u64.

Pipeline.EndRequest.note: Panics with 'out of sync' for the wrong id, as Go does.

Pipeline.EndResponse.note: Panics with 'out of sync' for the wrong id, as Go does.

ProtocolError.note: Newtype over String; Error::Protocol holds it.

ProtocolError.Error.note: impl Display for ProtocolError gives the message.

Reader.note: Generic over BufRead; every accumulating read is bounded by Limits. Defaults: line 1 MiB, header block 1 MiB, 10,000 headers, dot-encoded body 16 MiB, response 1 MiB. Go has no such bounds; the defaults are far above Go's own test inputs and the differential harness raises them.

Reader.ReadCodeLine.note: Returns Rust Strings: a message that is not valid UTF-8 is Error::InvalidUtf8 where Go returns the bytes.

Reader.ReadContinuedLine.note: A line that is not valid UTF-8 is Error::InvalidUtf8 where Go returns the bytes; read_continued_line_bytes has no such limit.

Reader.ReadDotLines.note: A line that is not valid UTF-8 is Error::InvalidUtf8 where Go returns the bytes; read_dot_bytes has no such limit.

Reader.ReadLine.note: A line that is not valid UTF-8 is Error::InvalidUtf8 where Go returns the bytes; read_line_bytes has no such limit.

Reader.ReadMIMEHeader.note: Header values are Strings, so non-UTF-8 bytes are Error::InvalidUtf8. Charged against Limits (default 1 MiB per header block, 10,000 headers) as Go's limited variant does, where Go's public method is unbounded.

Reader.ReadResponse.note: Returns a Rust String: a message that is not valid UTF-8 is Error::InvalidUtf8 where Go returns the bytes.

Writer.PrintfLine.note: Takes the line as impl Display; pass format_args! for Go's format and arguments.
